info.title: Voice OUT Rates
info.description:
JSONAPI interface to the Voice OUT prices of a DIDWW account: what outbound calls to each
destination cost, as priced by the plan the account is assigned to. The plan's whole price
list is one gzipped CSV file; one number is looked up directly. Prices are plan values in
USD, VAT excluded.

Every request is authenticated with a bearer access token (`Authorization: Bearer <token>`).
Mint one with `POST /token` on the token service of the environment you call —
`https://auth.didww.com/token` for Production, `https://auth-sandbox.didww.com/token` for
Sandbox — with an API key issued in the DIDWW user panel. The audience this service verifies
is `api-vout.didww.com` on the production and on the sandbox host alike, so the token's `aud`
must list that name. Every operation here reads: a token minted with the `read` scope is
enough.

An account with no plan assigned is answered with 404 `price_plan_not_assigned` by every
operation, and every operation spends the account's rate-limit budget: once it is spent,
the answer is 429 with `Retry-After`.

tags.name: Prices
tags.description: Price files and price lookups, served by the platform service that prices the traffic: Voice IN, Voice OUT, SMS.

bearer_token.description: Short-lived access token minted by `POST /token` on the token service of the environment you call — `https://auth.didww.com/token` for the Production servers, `https://auth-sandbox.didww.com/token` for the Sandbox servers — with an API key of that environment; a token minted in one environment is refused by the other. It is minted for an explicit set of audiences (`aud`). The audience of an operation is the production hostname of the server in effect for it — the Production entry of the operation's own `servers`, else of its path item's `servers` with the `service` variable resolved, else of the document's root `servers` — and it is the same name whether you call the production or the sandbox host. A service accepts a token only when `aud` lists its name: mint one token per service, or one token listing every service you call.

code.description: JSONAPI error code: a numeric code for a request-shape error (`100` a validation error, `102` a disallowed filter, `106` a missing parameter, and so on), the HTTP status for a refused token or scope (`401`, `403` — the reason is in `title` and in the `WWW-Authenticate` header), or a named code for a domain refusal or a serving failure (`price_plan_not_assigned`, `price_not_found`, `too_many_requests`, `serving_failure`).

source.description: Points at the part of the request that caused the error. Present on validation errors.

meta.description: Error-specific details. Carried by a few errors (e.g. insufficient balance).

id.description: UUID naming the answer by the plan, the prefix and the routing conditions, so a re-import of the same price keeps it. A name, not an address: there is no member route to fetch it by.

prefix.description: Destination prefix of the plan that priced the number: the longest one covering it among the prices of the same routing conditions. Its last digit can be a range in brackets: `123[4-8]` covers the numbers starting with 1234 to 1238 and ranks as four digits long.

country.description: Destination country of the prefix, by name; null when the prefix is not attributed to a country.

network.description: Destination network of the prefix, by name; null when the prefix is not attributed to a network.

rate.description: Per-minute rate in USD, VAT excluded, as a decimal string that is never rounded; null when `reject_calls` is set.

connection_fee.description: Fee charged once per call, in USD, VAT excluded, as a decimal string; null when `reject_calls` is set.

initial_increment.description: First billing increment, in seconds: a call is charged for at least this long. On a rejected destination about to open, the increment it opens with.

recurring_increment.description: Each following billing increment, in seconds. On a rejected destination about to open, the increment it opens with.

next_rate.description: Per-minute rate in USD, VAT excluded, from `next_rate_effective_at` on; null when no change is scheduled, when the price is removed, or when the destination is going to reject calls.

next_connection_fee.description: Fee charged once per call, in USD, VAT excluded, from `next_rate_effective_at` on; null whenever `next_rate` is.

next_rate_effective_at.description: When the change named by `next_change` takes effect; null when no change is scheduled.

next_change.description: The scheduled change of the price: `Increase` or `Decrease` of the rate, `Connection fee change`, `Billing increment change`, or two or three of these joined (`Increase and Connection fee change`); `No Change` when the next values equal the current ones; `Reject calls` when the destination is going to reject calls; `Removed` when the price ends within 30 days and no price of the same prefix takes over when it ends; `New Breakout` when a rejected destination opens within 30 days. Null when no change is scheduled.

reject_calls.description: True when the plan rejects calls to this destination instead of pricing them; `rate` and `connection_fee` are then null. A rejection is an answer, not a missing price.

category.description: Category of the price, as the sheets of the price list in the user panel group them. Rows of one lookup may share a category.

data.description: One answer per set of routing conditions of the plan whose prefixes cover the number. Never empty: no answer is the 404 `price_not_found`.

ContentDisposition.description: `attachment` with the canonical file name of the price domain.

ContentLength.description: Size of the gzipped file in bytes; a HEAD answers the size the download sends.

LastModified.description: HTTP date the file's content or the account's plan assignment last changed; the value to send back in `If-Modified-Since`.

CacheControl.description: Always `private`: the file is served per account.

AcceptRanges.description: Always `none`: the file is served whole.

Vary.description: Always `Authorization`: one URL answers every account with its own plan's file.

get.summary: Look up the price of a number
get.description: Looks up the price of one number in the plan assigned to the account. The number is matched against the destination prefixes of the plan: for every set of routing conditions the plan prices, the longest prefix covering the number answers, so the collection carries one row per such set and is never empty -- a number no prefix covers is a 404 (`price_not_found`). A prefix answers only while its price is in effect and only for a number whose length is within the bounds the plan sets for it; a change already scheduled is carried by the `next_` attributes and named by `next_change`. A destination the plan rejects is still an answer: `reject_calls` is true and `rate` and `connection_fee` are null. The token must list `api-vout.didww.com` in its audience, on the sandbox host as well; the `read` scope suffices. `filter` is the only query parameter read: `sort`, `page`, `fields`, `include` and anything unrecognised are refused with 400.

parameters.name: filter[number]
parameters.description: The number to price: 8 to 15 digits with a non-zero first digit, in international format without a `+` or a dialling prefix.

200.description: the prices covering the number: one per set of routing conditions, the longest covering prefix of each

400.description: malformed request: `filter[number]` missing or blank, or not 8 to 15 digits with a non-zero first digit; a filter other than `number`, `filter[id]` included; or any other query parameter -- `sort`, `page`, `fields`, `include` and anything unrecognised

401.description: the bearer token was refused: absent, malformed, expired, signed by a key this service does not hold, minted for another audience or environment, presented from an address outside the IP allowlist of the API key it was minted with, or naming an account this service has no record of; the response carries `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token"`

403.description: the token does not carry the `read` scope (title `Insufficient scope`); the response carries `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="insufficient_scope"`

404.description: no price plan is assigned to the account (`price_plan_not_assigned`), or no prefix of the plan covers the number (`price_not_found`)

429.description: the request budget of the account for the current window is spent (`too_many_requests`); `Retry-After` says how many seconds to wait

get.description: Downloads the price file of the plan assigned to the account: the prices of the plan as a gzipped CSV (UTF-8, LF line endings, a header row), named `voice_out_prices.csv.gz`. Prices are printed as the lookup answers them: never rounded, trailing zeros dropped, one decimal kept (`0.0`, `1.5`, `0.002`). One row per price of the plan, with the columns Category, Country, Network, Prefix, Rate (USD, excl. VAT), Connection fee (USD, excl. VAT), Initial Increment, Recurring Increment, Reject calls, Next rate (USD, excl. VAT), Next connection fee (USD, excl. VAT), Next rate effective date and Next change, carrying what the lookup's attributes of the matching names carry; the file leaves out some settings of a row, so two rows can look alike or show one prefix at different prices. The last digit of a prefix can be a range, as the lookup's `prefix` describes. A prefix with no price in effect whose next price starts within 30 days is also listed, with no Rate or Connection fee, as `New Breakout`. Prices are matched by the text of their prefix and their routing conditions, so a range that changes (`9995[0-5]` to `9995[0-7]`) is a new prefix: within 30 days of the change, the old one ends as `Removed` and the new one is listed as `New Breakout`. The file is small and served whole, with no byte ranges, and it is the account's own: `Cache-Control` is `private` and `Vary` is `Authorization`, so a cache keyed by the URL alone must not hand it to another account. The token must list `api-vout.didww.com` in its audience, on the sandbox host as well; the `read` scope suffices. Conditional requests use `Last-Modified` and `If-Modified-Since` only: no `ETag` is sent, and a request carrying `If-None-Match` is always answered in full, its `If-Modified-Since` ignored. `Last-Modified` is the later of the last change of the file's content and the last change of the account's plan assignment, so an account moved to another plan is never answered 304 with the prices it left; send it back in `If-Modified-Since` to be answered 304 while nothing has changed.

parameters.name: If-Modified-Since
parameters.description: The `Last-Modified` date of the copy you hold. The file is sent only if it changed after that date; otherwise the answer is 304. Ignored when the request also carries `If-None-Match`.

304.description: the file has not changed since the `If-Modified-Since` date: the headers of the 200 and no body

401.description: the bearer token was refused: absent, malformed, expired, signed by a key this service does not hold, minted for another audience or environment, presented from an address outside the IP allowlist of the API key it was minted with, or naming an account this service has no record of; the response carries `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token"`

403.description: the token does not carry the `read` scope (title `Insufficient scope`); the response carries `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="insufficient_scope"`

404.description: no price plan is assigned to the account (`price_plan_not_assigned`)

429.description: the request budget of the account for the current window is spent (`too_many_requests`); `Retry-After` says how many seconds to wait

503.description: the file could not be served: the assigned plan has no generated file yet, or the store did not answer for it (`serving_failure`); `Retry-After` says how many seconds to wait

head.description: Answers the headers of the price file without its body -- `Last-Modified`, `Content-Disposition` with `voice_out_prices.csv.gz`, `Content-Length` and the cache headers of the download -- so a client can tell whether its copy is current before downloading. `If-Modified-Since` works as on the download: a date at or after `Last-Modified` is answered 304, unless the request also carries `If-None-Match`. The audience (`api-vout.didww.com`, the same on the sandbox host), the scope (`read`) and the refusals are those of the download; no response carries a body.

parameters.name: If-Modified-Since
parameters.description: The `Last-Modified` date of the copy you hold. The headers of the file are answered only if it changed after that date; otherwise the answer is 304. Ignored when the request also carries `If-None-Match`.

200.description: the headers of the price file

304.description: the file has not changed since the `If-Modified-Since` date: the headers of the 200

401.description: the bearer token was refused: absent, malformed, expired, signed by a key this service does not hold, minted for another audience or environment, presented from an address outside the IP allowlist of the API key it was minted with, or naming an account this service has no record of; the response carries `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token"`

403.description: the token does not carry the `read` scope (title `Insufficient scope`); the response carries `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="insufficient_scope"`

404.description: no price plan is assigned to the account (`price_plan_not_assigned`)

429.description: the request budget of the account for the current window is spent (`too_many_requests`); `Retry-After` says how many seconds to wait

503.description: the file could not be served: the assigned plan has no generated file yet (`serving_failure`); `Retry-After` says how many seconds to wait
